loop_skills.name: flux-loop-commands
loop_skills.description: What a Flux loop's workers can read and run while the loop runs -- a coding agent inside a turn, a direct model with tools, or a step script (check, stage, generator, search, compose) -- plus the commands for reading a loop from outside. Use when writing a step or search script, when acting as an agent inside a Flux turn (PROMPT.md / BRIEF.md in the work directory), or when asked how a loop retrieves its ideas, previous attempts and designs, measured numbers, papers and digests, or how to run the gate or a stage on a file.

tasks.title: Clean scratch
tasks.what: Delete what Flux's temporary folder (FLUX_TMPDIR) holds that nothing has touched for a while and no process uses. Shared by everything on this machine: off until turned on.

tasks.title: Reap containers
tasks.what: Remove sandbox containers no process runs any more (D768).

tasks.title: Clean idle caches
tasks.what: A loop's sandbox cache (tools' caches and past passes' agent folders) when the loop has not run for a while.

tasks.title: Disk alert
tasks.what: Tell the admins when a disk the server uses has little space left.

tasks.title: Compact databases
tasks.what: Checkpoint, optimise and vacuum the server's database and every loop's record; a record's designs kept once (a running loop's too, a few rows at a time).

tasks.title: Condense run logs
tasks.what: A loop's log over a size keeps its recent part; the older part is gzipped beside it.

tasks.title: Prune server tables
tasks.what: Expired sessions and invitations, old login failures and notifications, and audit lines past their age.

tasks.title: Remove orphaned caches
tasks.what: A sandbox cache whose loop was deleted (Admin > Resources lists it as gone).

tasks.title: Prune run history
tasks.what: Each loop keeps its latest starts in the server's run list; older rows go (a running start never).

tasks.title: Bring task journals up to date
tasks.what: A loop's task journal written before the engine said what each task is (D1233) is rewritten in today's format, once, by the rules Live read it by: each task's box, pass, design and try, how each try ended, the bookkeeping as notes. The original is kept beside it (events.jsonl.orig.gz). A running loop is left until it stops.

tasks.title: Condense task journals
tasks.what: A loop's task journal (the Live tree's history) over a size keeps its recent starts whole; older ones are gzipped beside it.

tasks.title: Thin old transcripts
tasks.what: A loop's transcript (every model and agent turn: its prompt, reply and tool calls) keeps its last days whole; an older turn keeps only what usage counts -- when, who, tokens, cost, whether it failed and why. Insights reads the usage log, summed as turns happen. Running loops too: a turn is appended on its own.

tasks.title: Prune old agent folders
tasks.what: A loop's working folders of passes started more than the days ago (each agent's prompt, drafts and scratch) go -- its newest folder always stays, and the journal, the transcript, the record and the workbench. Running loops too: an old pass's folder is not written to.

tasks.title: Prune refused-host log
tasks.what: The sandbox proxies' log of refused connections keeps its last days (Insights > Network reads it).

tasks.title: Prune stale records
tasks.what: Record rows measured under other inputs (D853): the loop no longer counts them. Reports them; deletes them when told to.

tasks.title: Prune empty starts
tasks.what: Starts that did nothing -- stopped before any search, design, check or measurement began (D987) -- go: their row, and for a loop's latest start its log and journal. Starts already checked are left.

tasks.title: Rerun baseline
tasks.what: The loop's next start measures pass 0 again, once (D1005): otherwise a baseline on record stands while the document's baseline: section is unchanged, whatever else changed.

tasks.title: Invalidate + re-evaluate all
tasks.what: After the checks or measurement scripts change (D988): one run checks and measures every design on record again; the earlier results stay as history, no longer counted. Started on one loop only.

tasks.title: Check database integrity
tasks.what: Read-only SQLite integrity checks on the server database and stopped loops' out/*.db records. Reports problems without repairing or deleting data.

tasks.title: Validate loop documents
tasks.what: Load each stopped loop's selected problem document, including referenced parts. Reports errors without changing files or running tools or agents.

tasks.title: Back up server database
tasks.what: Save a consistent copy of flux-web.db and secret.key in the server data folder's backups/. Keep the latest backups, deleting older ones. Contains accounts, settings and run metadata; loop files, outputs and sandbox caches are not included.

applications.name: adder16
applications.statement: An unsigned 16-bit adder (module `adder16`, inputs `a` and `b`, 17-bit sum `s`): the smallest that makes 2900 MHz placed on ASAP7, chosen from the architectures gen.py spells.

applications.name: bankmap
applications.statement: An address-to-bank mapping for a memory of 8 banks that is conflict-free for 4 concurrent accesses at each of the strides 1, 8 and 16, for every start address of a 20-bit space: the cheapest one the exhaustive checker accepts, or the proof that none exists and what is achievable instead.

applications.name: macarray
applications.statement: One MAC processing element, 8 lanes at the workload's precision (int8 x int8, accumulated): the smallest PE that makes 1000 MHz placed on ASAP7, chosen from every combination of multiplier, reducer and pipeline depth the generator can spell, plus every multiplier the invention problem kept.

applications.name: mul8
applications.statement: A combinational signed 8x8 -> 16-bit multiplier in SystemVerilog: module `mul8` with inputs `a` and `w` (`input logic signed [7:0]`) and output `p` (`output logic signed [15:0]`), the smallest that makes 1600 MHz placed on ASAP7.

applications.name: nlu
applications.statement: The seven operators of an FP16 non-linear unit (recip, rsqrt, sigmoid, tanh, gelu, log, exp): each within 1 ULP of the correctly rounded reference on ALL 65536 inputs, at 800 MHz on ASAP7 with the least area and power.

applications.name: prefetcher
applications.statement: The L2 prefetcher configuration for 5G baseband workloads (FFT-heavy signal processing, channel-estimation matrix work, bursty packet buffers): Bingo, the partners that run beside it and their knobs. The fastest configuration by geomean IPC speedup over no prefetcher, then the smallest that holds 90% of that gain.

applications.name: primes
applications.statement: A Python function `count_primes(n: int) -> int` that returns how many primes are below n, as fast as possible for n up to 2,000,000.

applications.name: pto
applications.statement: One combinational datapath, in pyCircuit, for the PTO ISA's elementwise tile units: what a vector engine lane computes for one element. INTERFACE (fixed -- the checks drive exactly these ports): inputs `op` (8 bits: the unit, by its code from `fluxpreset pto ops --spec spec`), `dtype` (5 bits: the data type, by its position in the spec's TileDataType enumeration, listed by the same command), `a` and `b` (64 bits: the source elements in their low bits; one-source units ignore `b`); outputs `y` (64 bits: the destination element in its low bits -- only the type's width is compared) and `fault`…
